question: A 25-year old Caucasian female presents with symptoms of Graves' disease. Her doctor prescribes medications and sends the patient home. After two months of therapy, the patient returns upset that her exophthalmos has not gone away. Which of the following drugs should the physician have prescribed to treat the exophthalmos?

options.ope: No treatment as this will resolve naturally

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Graves' disease -> autoimmune thyroid disorder -> exophthalmos (bulging eyes) -> 90% CHAIN: Exophthalmos in Graves' disease -> caused by inflammation and swelling behind the eyes -> 80% CHAIN: Corticosteroids -> anti-inflammatory properties -> reduce inflammation and swelling -> potential treatment for exophthalmos in Graves' disease -> 70% CHAIN: PTU (Propylthiouracil) -> used to treat hyperthyroidism in Graves' disease -> may help improve exophthalmos indirectly by controlling thyroid hormone levels -> 60% CHAIN: Propanolol or Metoprolol -> beta-blockers -> may help manage symptoms like rapid heart rate and tremors in Graves' disease but not directly treat exophthalmos -> 50% CHAIN: No treatment -> exophthalmos may not resolve naturally in all cases -> 90%
analysis: Exophthalmos in Graves' disease is typically treated with corticosteroids to reduce inflammation and swelling around the eyes.
